<!-- Generated by dev/tools/gen-site-docs (internal/sitedoc). DO NOT EDIT: edit the command metadata / flag declarations / ledgers and re-run the generator. -->

`lookout audit` asks a different question from everything else: not "what
is broken" but **"what has no safety net, while it is still healthy"**. A
posture finding is a standing claim — it never self-clears, because a
workload with one replica has one replica until somebody decides
otherwise.

Reachable three ways: `lookout audit all -A` (every posture detector in one
pass over a shared cluster snapshot, stamping `check=<subcommand>`), the
individual subcommands below, or `lookout scan --include=audit` for the
whole sweep alongside the incident checks. Like `scan`, it needs nothing
deployed — a kubeconfig is the whole setup.

### Profiles, policy overlays, and exemptions

Posture claims depend on the cluster's role and platform, so every audit
command shares one rule-selection and exemption pipeline:

- **Profiles (`--profile=default|strict|onboarding|gke-autopilot`)** —
  built-in rule presets (e.g., `strict` promotes info-level hardening and
  reliability gaps to `warning`; `onboarding` focuses on high-signal
  blockers; `gke-autopilot` disables checks that Autopilot enforces at
  admission).
- **Declarative policy (`--policy=<file>`) & CLI overrides** — per-kind
  enablement, severity overrides, and threshold `params` in git-reviewed
  YAML, composable with `--only`, `--skip`, `--min-severity`, and `--set`.
  Run [`lookout audit policy`](/reference/audit-policy/) to inspect the
  effective rule table and provenance before scanning.
- **Scope & holder attribution** — `--skip-system-namespaces` omits
  platform-managed namespaces from cluster-wide sweeps, and `--per-workload`
  expands shared ServiceAccount/RBAC/PSA findings (`workloads`,
  `workload_names`) into one record per affected workload.
- **Auditable opt-outs (`--exemptions=<file>`)** — when the answer to a
  posture claim is "yes, deliberately", a git-reviewed exemption file
  records the reason and an expiry instead of the finding quietly
  disappearing. Covered findings are **annotated** with their reason and
  counted as `exempt=<n>`, never dropped, and
  [`lookout audit exemptions`](/reference/audit-exemptions/) audits the
  exemption file itself for expired or expiring entries.

## [`lookout audit ai`](/reference/audit-ai/)

Inference-workload security and scheduling posture across workload templates: serving Services in namespaces with no ingress NetworkPolicy isolating the model endpoint, hostNetwork on accelerator workloads, hostPath model-cache volumes, default ServiceAccount token automount on accelerator workloads, and unpinned model-loader or inference images. Scope with --namespace, -A, or --workload.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.ai_workload_exposure` | warning, info | an AI/inference workload has an unisolated serving Service, hostNetwork with accelerators, a hostPath model-cache mount, an automounted default ServiceAccount token, or an unpinned model-loader/inference container image |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## [`lookout audit all`](/reference/audit-all/)

Run every posture detector in one pass over a shared cluster snapshot: workload availability and rollout safety (`audit workloads`), container and Pod Security hardening (`audit hardening`), RBAC over-permission (`audit rbac`), NetworkPolicy coverage (`audit netpol`), provider cluster configuration (`audit cluster`) and upgrade readiness (`audit upgrades`), plus exemption hygiene (`audit exemptions`) when --exemptions is given. Shared Kubernetes resources are listed at most once across all detectors; each finding carries check=\<subcommand>. Scope with --namespace or -A.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.check_skipped` | info | a stage declined this invocation because a zero-argument scan cannot supply something it needs — the coverage claim is smaller than it looks |
| `scan.check_failed` | warning | a stage errored; the scan continued without it, so this run saw less than a whole cluster — unless EVERY stage failed and none read anything, which is a runtime error (exit 1) rather than a scan |
| `audit.no_pdb` | warning | the workload has no PodDisruptionBudget: a drain can take every replica at once |
| `audit.pdb_posture` | warning | a PodDisruptionBudget overlaps another PDB on the same workload or allows zero disruptions by spec, permanently blocking voluntary node drains |
| `audit.single_replica` | warning | the workload runs a single replica, so any disruption is an outage |
| `audit.no_readiness_probe` | warning | a container has no readiness probe, so traffic reaches it before it can serve |
| `audit.no_liveness_probe` | info | a container has no liveness probe, so a wedged process is never restarted |
| `audit.no_startup_probe` | warning, info | a container has a livenessProbe and no startupProbe, with either a liveness deadline under 60s (info) or a readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds >= 30s (warning) that shows slow startup is expected |
| `audit.no_resource_requests` | warning | a container has no CPU or memory request (and no limit or namespace LimitRange to default it from), so the scheduler places it blind and node eviction ranks it first |
| `audit.no_resource_limits` | warning, info | a container has no memory or CPU limit (and no namespace LimitRange default): an unbounded memory leak OOMs the node (warning), while an unbounded CPU spike is throttled only by contention (info) |
| `audit.no_spread` | info | the workload's replicas are not spread across nodes or zones |
| `audit.rigid_scheduling` | warning, info | placement constraints pin the workload to too few nodes to survive losing one |
| `audit.hpa_cannot_scale` | warning, info | the autoscaler structurally cannot scale or drops HA at idle: min equals max, the target is missing, a container has no request for its utilization target to divide by, or minReplicas is 1 |
| `audit.suspended_cronjob` | warning | a CronJob has been suspended past --cron-suspended and has skipped activations because of it: whatever it does is not happening, and nothing else reports that |
| `audit.cronjob_overlap_risk` | warning, info | a CronJob permits concurrent runs without an activeDeadlineSeconds bounding them to the schedule interval, or sets startingDeadlineSeconds below the controller's 10s check loop |
| `audit.cronjob_failing` | warning | an active CronJob has scheduled runs, none are currently running, and status.lastSuccessfulTime is nil — it has never succeeded |
| `audit.suspended_job` | info | a standalone Job (no controller owner, not queued by Kueue) has been suspended past --job-suspended without finishing: the one-shot task it carries is not happening |
| `audit.liveness_preempts_readiness` | warning, info | liveness and readiness probe the same handler and liveness gives up no later than readiness: the kubelet restarts the container before readiness can take it out of the Service, so the readiness probe is decoration; info when the two deadlines tie, warning when liveness is strictly earlier |
| `audit.rollout_drops_traffic` | warning | a Service-backed, multi-replica workload (or a Service-backed DaemonSet) whose serving container has no preStop hook, or a container whose preStop sleep reaches or exceeds terminationGracePeriodSeconds: SIGTERM races endpoint removal or SIGKILL arrives with zero drain time |
| `audit.recreate_strategy` | warning | a Service-backed, multi-replica Deployment whose strategy permits zero surviving pods — Recreate, or rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable at or above the replica count — so every rollout is an outage the Deployment never reports |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |
| `audit.privileged_container` | warning | a container runs privileged or holds a node-root capability (ALL, SYS_ADMIN): a container escape is a node compromise |
| `audit.host_namespace` | warning | the pod shares the node's network, PID, or IPC namespace |
| `audit.hostpath_mount` | warning, info | the pod mounts a host path; warning when it is writable, info when read-only |
| `audit.default_sa_automount` | warning | the pod runs as the namespace's default ServiceAccount with its token automounted, and something in the pod can use it |
| `audit.sa_token_automount` | info | the pod runs as a non-default ServiceAccount with its token automounted, but no RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding binds that ServiceAccount |
| `audit.container_security_gaps` | warning, info | a non-privileged container runs as UID 0, leaves runAsNonRoot unset, permits privilege escalation, or has no RuntimeDefault/Localhost seccomp profile |
| `audit.writable_rootfs` | info | a container does not set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, so the root filesystem is writable at runtime |
| `audit.capabilities_added` | warning, info | a container adds Linux capabilities below node-root (NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW, SYS_PTRACE, ...) or does not drop ALL default capabilities |
| `audit.podsecurity_gaps` | warning | the namespace enforces no Pod Security Admission level, so none of the above is prevented |
| `audit.image_floating_tag` | info | a container image reference names no particular bytes — a tag that by convention moves (latest, main, master, dev, nightly, stable, edge) or no tag at all, with no digest: the next pull may run different code with no deploy and no record |
| `audit.cluster_admin_binding` | warning, info | the binding grants a full-wildcard role (cluster-admin, or one with the same rule) to its subjects; warning for a ClusterRoleBinding, info for a RoleBinding, which confines it to one namespace |
| `audit.wildcard_rbac` | warning, info | the role has a rule using `*` for verbs or resources; warning for a full wildcard that something binds, info for an unbound one and for the narrower wildcards |
| `audit.exec_attach_grant` | warning, info | the binding grants pods/exec, pods/attach, or pods/portforward to its subjects; warning for exec or attach, info for portforward |
| `audit.impersonate_escalate_grant` | warning | the binding grants impersonate on identities or bind/escalate on RBAC roles to its subjects |
| `audit.netpol_missing` | warning, info | nothing restricts this direction for the subject — a namespace with no policy at all, or a workload the covering policies' selectors miss; info for the egress direction, where no policy is a defensible default |
| `audit.netpol_selects_nothing` | warning | this NetworkPolicy's podSelector matches no workload in its namespace, so neither its isolation nor its allow rules apply to anything; reported only where the namespace claim does not already say the namespace's policies select nothing |
| `audit.network_policy_allow_all` | warning, info | this NetworkPolicy has an allow-all peer rule (empty from/to peer list, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 without except, or an empty namespaceSelector with no podSelector); warning for ingress, info for egress |
| `audit.no_resource_quota` | warning, info | workload-bearing namespace has no ResourceQuota or a ResourceQuota is >= 90% of hard limit |
| `audit.no_limit_range` | info | workload-bearing namespace has no LimitRange while containers omit resource requests/limits |
| `audit.namespace_onboarding_gaps` | warning, info | workload-bearing namespace is missing required onboarding labels |
| `audit.workload_identity_off` | warning | Workload Identity is off cluster-wide, or a node pool bypasses it — pods authenticate to the cloud as the node |
| `audit.legacy_metadata` | warning | a node pool still serves the pre-v1 instance-metadata endpoints, which any pod can read |
| `audit.public_control_plane` | warning, info | the control-plane endpoint is reachable from the internet; info when authorized networks narrow it |
| `audit.nodepool_cannot_grow` | warning | a node pool has autoscaling on with a maximum of 0 nodes: it can never hold a node, so a pod only it could host stays Pending forever |
| `audit.cluster_security_posture` | warning, info | cluster-level security posture gap: Shielded Nodes disabled, Binary Authorization disabled, application-layer etcd secrets encryption disabled, or legacy ABAC enabled |
| `audit.cluster_network_posture` | warning, info | cluster-level network posture gap: nodes carry public IPs, Dataplane V2 is disabled, or master global access is off on a private control-plane endpoint |
| `audit.cluster_observability_off` | warning, info | cluster-level observability disabled: Cloud Logging, Cloud Monitoring, or Managed Service for Prometheus is turned off |
| `audit.cluster_backup_off` | info | Backup for GKE addon is disabled on the cluster |
| `cloud.unavailable` | info | the cloud capability this check needs is unavailable, so nothing was examined — an explicit degradation record, never silence |
| `audit.version_behind` | critical, warning, info | the control plane or a node pool is behind what the provider publishes, or a node pool has skewed from the control plane; info while the gap is still within the supported skew |
| `audit.upgrade_unmanaged` | warning | nothing will close that gap on its own: no release channel, or node auto-upgrade/auto-repair off |
| `audit.upgrade_blocked` | critical, warning, info | an active maintenance exclusion, a node image on the removed Docker runtime, a removed API in use, a fail-closed upgrade-path webhook, or a zero-disruption PDB will stop or stall the upgrade when it comes |
| `audit.deprecated_api_in_use` | critical, warning | a cluster resource was last applied with a Kubernetes API version that is deprecated or removed in the target minor release |
| `audit.upgrade_unattended` | info | upgrades will happen with nobody watching: no maintenance window, or no upgrade notifications |
| `audit.exemption_expired` | warning | an exemption entry has lapsed: the findings it used to annotate are being reported unqualified again |
| `audit.exemption_expiring` | info | an exemption entry lapses within --within — renew it or let it go deliberately |
| `audit.compute_class_posture` | warning, info | a workload's GKE ComputeClass or hardware-placement spec has no fallback or cannot be satisfied by the cluster: references a non-existent ComputeClass, requests a class or accelerator with zero matching nodes and no node-pool auto-creation, pins multi-replica pods directly to Spot without a ComputeClass priority fallback chain, or pins an accelerator workload to a zone with zero matching accelerator nodes while other zones have them |
| `audit.single_zone_nodepool` | warning, info | a multi-node pool has all of its nodes in a single availability zone while the cluster spans multiple zones, or a workload with zone topologySpreadConstraints is pinned to a single-zone node pool |
| `audit.ai_workload_exposure` | warning, info | an AI/inference workload has an unisolated serving Service, hostNetwork with accelerators, a hostPath model-cache mount, an automounted default ServiceAccount token, or an unpinned model-loader/inference container image |

## [`lookout audit cluster`](/reference/audit-cluster/)

Cluster-level configuration posture, read from the cloud provider: Workload Identity off cluster-wide or bypassed by a node pool, node pools still serving the legacy metadata endpoints, a control-plane endpoint the internet can reach with nothing narrowing it, and a node pool whose autoscaler can never add a node. Reads the provider's cluster record, not Kubernetes objects, so it takes no --namespace/-A/--workload; scanned counts the cluster plus its node pools. Without a provider capability it reports an explicit unavailable rather than silence.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.workload_identity_off` | warning | Workload Identity is off cluster-wide, or a node pool bypasses it — pods authenticate to the cloud as the node |
| `audit.legacy_metadata` | warning | a node pool still serves the pre-v1 instance-metadata endpoints, which any pod can read |
| `audit.public_control_plane` | warning, info | the control-plane endpoint is reachable from the internet; info when authorized networks narrow it |
| `audit.nodepool_cannot_grow` | warning | a node pool has autoscaling on with a maximum of 0 nodes: it can never hold a node, so a pod only it could host stays Pending forever |
| `audit.cluster_security_posture` | warning, info | cluster-level security posture gap: Shielded Nodes disabled, Binary Authorization disabled, application-layer etcd secrets encryption disabled, or legacy ABAC enabled |
| `audit.cluster_network_posture` | warning, info | cluster-level network posture gap: nodes carry public IPs, Dataplane V2 is disabled, or master global access is off on a private control-plane endpoint |
| `audit.cluster_observability_off` | warning, info | cluster-level observability disabled: Cloud Logging, Cloud Monitoring, or Managed Service for Prometheus is turned off |
| `audit.cluster_backup_off` | info | Backup for GKE addon is disabled on the cluster |
| `cloud.unavailable` | info | the cloud capability this check needs is unavailable, so nothing was examined — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## [`lookout audit computeclass`](/reference/audit-computeclass/)

GKE ComputeClass, hardware-placement, and node-pool zone posture: workloads referencing a non-existent ComputeClass (`ComputeClassMissing`), workloads requesting a compute class or accelerator that matches zero nodes without node-pool auto-creation (`ComputeClassNoMatchingNodes`), multi-replica workloads pinned directly to Spot nodes without a ComputeClass fallback chain (`SpotWithoutFallback`), accelerator workloads pinned to a zone that hosts no matching accelerator nodes while other zones do (`UnsatisfiableZoneWithAccelerator`), and multi-node pools confined to a single availability zone (`SingleZoneNodePool`). Scope with --namespace, -A, or --workload.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.compute_class_posture` | warning, info | a workload's GKE ComputeClass or hardware-placement spec has no fallback or cannot be satisfied by the cluster: references a non-existent ComputeClass, requests a class or accelerator with zero matching nodes and no node-pool auto-creation, pins multi-replica pods directly to Spot without a ComputeClass priority fallback chain, or pins an accelerator workload to a zone with zero matching accelerator nodes while other zones have them |
| `audit.single_zone_nodepool` | warning, info | a multi-node pool has all of its nodes in a single availability zone while the cluster spans multiple zones, or a workload with zone topologySpreadConstraints is pinned to a single-zone node pool |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## [`lookout audit exemptions`](/reference/audit-exemptions/)

Audit the exemption file itself: which reviewed exemptions have lapsed (and are therefore no longer annotating anything) and which are about to. The mechanism that keeps an exemption file from becoming a permanent, unread list of things nobody checks any more.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.exemption_expired` | warning | an exemption entry has lapsed: the findings it used to annotate are being reported unqualified again |
| `audit.exemption_expiring` | info | an exemption entry lapses within --within — renew it or let it go deliberately |

Workload security posture: containers running privileged or holding node-root capabilities, pods sharing the host network/PID/IPC namespaces, hostPath mounts, default-ServiceAccount tokens that something actually uses, and namespaces with no Pod Security Admission enforcement. Judges every pod-template owner in scope — Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, CronJobs, unowned Jobs and unowned Pods — plus the namespaces around them. Scope with --namespace or -A; scanned counts pod templates examined, the namespaces note counts namespaces.

## [`lookout audit netpol`](/reference/audit-netpol/)

NetworkPolicy coverage posture: namespaces where nothing restricts ingress or egress at all, and individual workloads that fell through the selectors of the policies covering their neighbours, and individual policies whose selector matches no workload at all. Coverage means isolation — some policy selects the pod and names the direction — not that the rules it then applies are tight. hostNetwork templates are excluded, since NetworkPolicy cannot constrain them. Scope with --namespace or -A; scanned counts pod templates examined.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.netpol_missing` | warning, info | nothing restricts this direction for the subject — a namespace with no policy at all, or a workload the covering policies' selectors miss; info for the egress direction, where no policy is a defensible default |
| `audit.netpol_selects_nothing` | warning | this NetworkPolicy's podSelector matches no workload in its namespace, so neither its isolation nor its allow rules apply to anything; reported only where the namespace claim does not already say the namespace's policies select nothing |
| `audit.network_policy_allow_all` | warning, info | this NetworkPolicy has an allow-all peer rule (empty from/to peer list, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 without except, or an empty namespaceSelector with no podSelector); warning for ingress, info for egress |

## [`lookout audit rbac`](/reference/audit-rbac/)

RBAC over-permission posture: bindings that grant cluster-admin, or a role whose rules are cluster-admin under another name, and Roles/ClusterRoles whose rules use `*` for verbs or resources. Judges a binding by the rules of the role it points at, not by the role's name. Objects the platform reconciles (the bootstrap defaults, addon-manager Reconcile objects) are counted, not reported. --namespace judges that namespace's Roles and RoleBindings; ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings are judged under -A. scanned counts bindings and roles examined.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.cluster_admin_binding` | warning, info | the binding grants a full-wildcard role (cluster-admin, or one with the same rule) to its subjects; warning for a ClusterRoleBinding, info for a RoleBinding, which confines it to one namespace |
| `audit.wildcard_rbac` | warning, info | the role has a rule using `*` for verbs or resources; warning for a full wildcard that something binds, info for an unbound one and for the narrower wildcards |
| `audit.exec_attach_grant` | warning, info | the binding grants pods/exec, pods/attach, or pods/portforward to its subjects; warning for exec or attach, info for portforward |
| `audit.impersonate_escalate_grant` | warning | the binding grants impersonate on identities or bind/escalate on RBAC roles to its subjects |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## [`lookout audit upgrades`](/reference/audit-upgrades/)

Upgrade and patch readiness, read from the cloud provider and cluster upgrade-blocker catalogue: how far the control plane and its node pools are behind what the provider publishes (or --target-version), whether anything is set up to close that gap on its own — release channel, node auto-upgrade and auto-repair, a maintenance window, active maintenance exclusions, node images on the removed Docker runtime, and upgrade notifications — plus in-cluster upgrade blockers (deprecated/removed APIs in use, fail-closed admission webhooks on upgrade-critical paths, and PodDisruptionBudgets that allow zero disruptions during node drain). Without a provider capability or --target-version it reports an explicit unavailable rather than silence.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.version_behind` | critical, warning, info | the control plane or a node pool is behind what the provider publishes, or a node pool has skewed from the control plane; info while the gap is still within the supported skew |
| `audit.upgrade_unmanaged` | warning | nothing will close that gap on its own: no release channel, or node auto-upgrade/auto-repair off |
| `audit.upgrade_blocked` | critical, warning, info | an active maintenance exclusion, a node image on the removed Docker runtime, a removed API in use, a fail-closed upgrade-path webhook, or a zero-disruption PDB will stop or stall the upgrade when it comes |
| `audit.deprecated_api_in_use` | critical, warning | a cluster resource was last applied with a Kubernetes API version that is deprecated or removed in the target minor release |
| `audit.upgrade_unattended` | info | upgrades will happen with nobody watching: no maintenance window, or no upgrade notifications |
| `cloud.unavailable` | info | the cloud capability this check needs is unavailable, so nothing was examined — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## [`lookout audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/)

Workload reliability posture for workloads that are healthy right now: no PodDisruptionBudget, only one replica, no readiness/liveness probe, no spread across nodes, placement pinned to too few nodes, autoscalers that structurally cannot scale, CronJobs left suspended long enough to have skipped runs, standalone Jobs left suspended past a maintenance window, and the rollout-safety claims for Service-backed workloads: liveness probes that fire before readiness on the same handler, serving containers with no preStop hook, and Deployment strategies that permit zero surviving pods. Answers "what has no safety net", as against `stab drain`, which answers "what breaks if I drain THIS node now". Scope with --namespace, -A, or --workload; scanned counts workloads examined.

| Kind | Severity | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.no_pdb` | warning | the workload has no PodDisruptionBudget: a drain can take every replica at once |
| `audit.pdb_posture` | warning | a PodDisruptionBudget overlaps another PDB on the same workload or allows zero disruptions by spec, permanently blocking voluntary node drains |
| `audit.single_replica` | warning | the workload runs a single replica, so any disruption is an outage |
| `audit.no_readiness_probe` | warning | a container has no readiness probe, so traffic reaches it before it can serve |
| `audit.no_liveness_probe` | info | a container has no liveness probe, so a wedged process is never restarted |
| `audit.no_startup_probe` | warning, info | a container has a livenessProbe and no startupProbe, with either a liveness deadline under 60s (info) or a readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds >= 30s (warning) that shows slow startup is expected |
| `audit.no_resource_requests` | warning | a container has no CPU or memory request (and no limit or namespace LimitRange to default it from), so the scheduler places it blind and node eviction ranks it first |
| `audit.no_resource_limits` | warning, info | a container has no memory or CPU limit (and no namespace LimitRange default): an unbounded memory leak OOMs the node (warning), while an unbounded CPU spike is throttled only by contention (info) |
| `audit.no_spread` | info | the workload's replicas are not spread across nodes or zones |
| `audit.rigid_scheduling` | warning, info | placement constraints pin the workload to too few nodes to survive losing one |
| `audit.hpa_cannot_scale` | warning, info | the autoscaler structurally cannot scale or drops HA at idle: min equals max, the target is missing, a container has no request for its utilization target to divide by, or minReplicas is 1 |
| `audit.suspended_cronjob` | warning | a CronJob has been suspended past --cron-suspended and has skipped activations because of it: whatever it does is not happening, and nothing else reports that |
| `audit.cronjob_overlap_risk` | warning, info | a CronJob permits concurrent runs without an activeDeadlineSeconds bounding them to the schedule interval, or sets startingDeadlineSeconds below the controller's 10s check loop |
| `audit.cronjob_failing` | warning | an active CronJob has scheduled runs, none are currently running, and status.lastSuccessfulTime is nil — it has never succeeded |
| `audit.suspended_job` | info | a standalone Job (no controller owner, not queued by Kueue) has been suspended past --job-suspended without finishing: the one-shot task it carries is not happening |
| `audit.liveness_preempts_readiness` | warning, info | liveness and readiness probe the same handler and liveness gives up no later than readiness: the kubelet restarts the container before readiness can take it out of the Service, so the readiness probe is decoration; info when the two deadlines tie, warning when liveness is strictly earlier |
| `audit.rollout_drops_traffic` | warning | a Service-backed, multi-replica workload (or a Service-backed DaemonSet) whose serving container has no preStop hook, or a container whose preStop sleep reaches or exceeds terminationGracePeriodSeconds: SIGTERM races endpoint removal or SIGKILL arrives with zero drain time |
| `audit.recreate_strategy` | warning | a Service-backed, multi-replica Deployment whose strategy permits zero surviving pods — Recreate, or rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable at or above the replica count — so every rollout is an outage the Deployment never reports |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |
